items.title: Hormuz is the biggest risk to the business
items.facts: Traffic is about 5% of normal (around 4 ships a day vs 85), tankers were attacked again this week and war-risk insurance is about 32 times normal. Every ore cargo in and every pellet or steel cargo out through the strait is exposed.
items.decision: Approve extra ore stock and pre-booked Q1 freight and insurance; ask for a plan B route (ports outside the strait, the GCC railway).

items.title: Saudi Arabia is investigating section imports
items.facts: Saudi Arabia opened an anti-dumping investigation into hot-rolled sections from China and Türkiye. If duties follow, our main competitors in our biggest regional market become more expensive. EMSTEEL is already supplying sections to energy projects.
items.decision: Support the case with data and get sales ready to grow Saudi section volumes.

items.title: Gas is now a strategic risk, not just a cost
items.facts: Egypt cut gas to its steel mills (Ezz Steel lost 30%) and Italian mills stopped on energy costs. Our DRP and meltshop depend on gas in the same way.
items.decision: Review how secure our gas contract is; meanwhile offer billets, sections or HBI into Egypt and southern Europe.

items.title: Pellet supply is tight while iron ore is cheap
items.facts: Ferrexpo has stopped pellet production in Ukraine, supporting European pellet premiums. Iron ore is near a 2-year low (about $91) and Simandou has started producing.
items.decision: Lock in ore purchases at today's low prices and offer pellets to the European buyers Ferrexpo supplied.

items.title: Green-steel demand in Europe is slower but coming
items.facts: thyssenkrupp's DRI plant slipped to 2029, POSCO's new EAF runs at 10% of capacity, and EU carbon border (CBAM) costs are rising for Indian exporters.
items.decision: Use the extra time to sign DR-pellet supply deals early and prepare product carbon footprints; our gas-DRI route is an advantage under CBAM.

items.title: Europe is closing its steel market (to confirm)
items.facts: A report says out-of-quota EU tariffs rise to 50%, which could cut imports by 47%. Flagged by keyword rules only, not yet reviewed.
items.decision: Ask the team to confirm before acting on it.

also: Deadly crane-and-furnace blast at Habaş, Türkiye: run a quick safety check of our meltshop cranes.
Chinese steel exports are down 2.3% this year but expected to rebound: watch Chinese sections coming into the GCC.
questions: How many weeks of ore stock do we hold, and what is the plan if Hormuz stays shut?
